before.name: Tyre is founded in 2750 BC (according to Herodotus)

after.name: c. 2750 BC: Traditional founding of Tyre, based on priests’ account to Herodotus; date uncertain

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Herodotus Histories 2.44 reports local priests said their temple was founded with the city 2300 years before his visit. The overview infers c.2750 BCE; neither the ancient report nor the calculation independently establishes an exact founding date or a treaty. The coordinate refers to modern Tyre and radius is a game setting, not the exact bounds of an Early Bronze Age settlement. Herodotus lived in the fifth century BCE, not in 2750 BCE.

The nearby Dhaskalio site is Early Cycladic, not demonstrated Minoan; the Minoan hint was unsupported and removed. The existing -4000..-1999 occupation bounds and town rank have NOT been verified and remain unchanged to avoid an unsupported reconstruction. Empty hint does not guarantee no other fallback will label it Minoan; saved states untested.

event.name: c. 2750–2550 BC: Keros and Dhaskalio early archaeological phase, dates approximate

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Keros and neighbouring Dhaskalio: researchers model an early settlement/deposition phase roughly 2750–2550 BCE. Bayesian start estimates have wide ranges (2012 paper table reports 95% beginning intervals including 2885–2622 BCE in one model). Broken marble objects at Kavos are interpreted as a ritual deposit; do not assume a known deity, exact annual use, or that every later monumental building existed at phase start. The point represents Dhaskalio; radius covers Kavos as a local reference, not a territory. NewsIndex may repeat the note every year.
